To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) a network with one hidden layer and 100 hidden nodes trained with a Levenberg-Marquardt algorithm and a 10-day training set has the lowest MAPE; (2) a network with two hidden layers trained with a Leveberg-Marquardl algorithm has the highest accuracy; and (3) the addition of a data set to the training set does not improve the forecast.

a network trained with 2 years of load data, a single hidden layer, and the Levenberg-Marquardt algorithm gives the best forecast, and the addition to the network of data that includes the current month's data does not improve the forecast.

(1) the best algorithm for short term load forecasting in the ERCOT system is a multilayer perceptron, (2) the best combination of hidden layer size, hidden layer number, and training set length for the multilayer perceptrons is 10, 1, 30, respectively, and (3) the best combination for the radial basis function neural network is 10,2, 30.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following questions: (1) How does the accuracy of a forecast generated by a NN change when the size of the training set is varied? (2) How does the number of hidden layers affect the accuracy of the forecast?
the best way to train a neural network to generate a forecast with the lowest MAPE.
the best possible NN configuration to generate a forecast that is accurate enough to be used by the power system operators.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the MAPE is lowest when the NN uses a Levenberg-Marquardt algorithm, a 1 hidden layer, and the training set is at least 2 years in length.
the best forecast accuracy is obtained with the following: a) using a Levenberg-Marquardt (LM) trained NN, b) a training set of 2 years, c) a 2-layer NN with 20 neurons in the hidden layer.

a NN with 2 hidden layers and a training set of the past 7 days of load data, trained using the Levenberg-Marquardt (LM) algorithm, and with the past 30 days of load data added to the network as a second data set for training, gives the most accurate forecast for a day ahead of the current time.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we were able to decrease the MAPE of our forecasts by over 30%, and we were able to generate a forecast that had an MAPE of 0.5% for a 24-hour forecast.

the NN algorithm used, the number of training days used in the training set, and the size and number of hidden layers all affect the accuracy of the forecast, but the addition of a new dataset does not improve the accuracy of the NN's forecast.
the MAPE of a forecast can be decreased by adding more training data to the network, increasing the hidden layer size, and using the back propagation algorithm.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the best combination of factors is a network trained with the Levenberg-Marquardt algorithm, with a training set that includes data from the past 12 months, with a hidden layer size of 100, with 2 hidden layers, and with the addition of the historical load data of the previous 12 months to the training set.

a NN trained using the Levenberg-Marquardt algorithm, with a training set of one year of load data, a hidden layer size of 10 nodes, and a hidden layer of one is able to produce a forecast with the lowest MAPE.

a deep NN with a large training set and multiple hidden layers is the most effective at forecasting the system load in ERCOT, and that adding additional data sets does not improve the accuracy of the NN.
